title: Webster votes to pass national security funding bill with reduced spending
text:
Webster votes to pass national security funding bill with reduced spending
Florida Congressman Daniel Webster announced on July 15 that he voted to pass H.R. 8595, the Fiscal Year 2027 National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act. The legislation aims to reduce spending by six percent while maintaining investments in national security priorities.
“This legislation rejects the Washington presumption that nothing can be cut from the budget in order to fund our nation’s priorities without increasing the deficit,” said Daniel Webster. “Through regular order, we are advancing America First policies that strengthen our national security, support key allies, confront our adversaries, and eliminate wasteful spending on programs that do not serve America’s interests. While there is more work to be done to restore fiscal discipline, this bill is an important step toward ensuring our national security and foreign policy priorities are accountable to the American people.”
According to Webster's office, the appropriations act includes provisions such as supporting allies like Israel and Taiwan, funding efforts against Chinese influence in the Indo-Pacific region, strengthening efforts against fentanyl trafficking and transnational crime, preserving pro-life protections, blocking funding for diversity mandates and certain international organizations including UNRWA and UNFPA, and enhancing oversight of taxpayer-funded foreign assistance.
Daniel Webster has represented Florida’s 11th district in Congress since 2011 after serving previously in both chambers of Florida's legislature, according to his official biography. He was born in Charleston, West Virginia in 1949 and resides in Clermont. Webster graduated from Georgia Institute of Technology with a Bachelor of Science degree.
